content.json:
# Log Analytics V1 Table Migration & DCR Wizard
This workbook inventories Log Analytics custom tables, migrates **Classic / V1** tables so they can receive DCR-based ingestion, discovers DCRs already targeting each table, and generates a replacement DCR for the **Logs Ingestion API** without changing the destination table's existing column names.

It does this by:
1. Reading the table's *current* columns (which typically have legacy type-suffixes like `Computer_s`, `EventTime_t`).
2. Building a DCR **input stream** using *clean* column names when they are unambiguous (suffix removed, e.g. `Computer`, `EventTime`).
3. Adding a **transformation** (`project-rename`) that renames the clean input columns back to the original suffixed names, so the **output stream** matches the table's existing schema exactly - **no destination table changes required**. If suffix removal creates duplicate names, the wizard automatically uses the original unique column names in compatibility mode.

> Table migration is one-way. Reference: [Custom logs migration guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/custom-logs-migrate) | [Data collection rule structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/essentials/data-collection-rule-structure) | [Data collection transformations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/essentials/data-collection-transformations)

**Legacy column suffix map** used to compute the clean input-stream column names and their DCR data types:

| Suffix | Legacy meaning | DCR / KQL type |
|---|---|---|
| `_s` | string | `string` |
| `_d` | number (double) | `real` |
| `_b` | boolean | `boolean` |
| `_g` | guid | `string` (Logs ingestion API stores/queries GUIDs as string) |
| `_t` | datetime | `datetime` |

Columns without a recognized suffix (e.g. `TimeGenerated`) are passed through unchanged. Reserved system columns (`_ResourceId`, `TenantId`, `Type`, `RawData`, etc.) are excluded automatically.

### Workflow
**1. Select a table**  ->  **2. Migrate / verify**  ->  **3. Inspect schema & existing DCRs**  ->  **4. Configure**  ->  **5. Review and deploy**

This is a single, always-loaded workspace. Later sections unlock automatically as you complete each stage, so your selections remain available while you review or change earlier choices.

# 1 | Select a custom table
Choose a workspace, compare migration and DCR status, then select a table.

## 1. Connect & inventory custom tables
The inventory includes **Classic** tables that require migration and DCR-based custom tables that might already have been migrated. Matching DCRs are correlated by output stream *and* workspace destination. This prevents a migrated table from disappearing from the wizard after its subtype changes.

parameters.name: Subscriptions
parameters.query:
resources
| where type =~ "microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces"
| distinct subscriptionId

parameters.name: Workspace
parameters.query:
resources
| where type =~ "microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces"
| project id, name, subscriptionId, location
| join kind = inner (
    resourcecontainers
    | where type == "microsoft.resources/subscriptions"
    | project subscriptionId, subscription = strcat(name," (",subscriptionId,")")
    )
on subscriptionId
| project value = id, label = name, group = subscription

parameters.name: TimeRange
parameters.label: Time Range
parameters.description: Used to evaluate ingestion volume and last-ingested time per table

parameters.name: ResourceGroupId
parameters.query:
resources
| where id =~ "{Workspace}"
| project value = strcat("/subscriptions/", subscriptionId, "/resourceGroups/", resourceGroup)

parameters.name: WorkspaceLocation
parameters.query:
resources
| where id =~ "{Workspace}"
| project value = location

parameters.name: WorkspaceCustomerId
parameters.query:
resources
| where id =~ "{Workspace}"
| project value = tostring(properties.customerId)

content.query:
resources
| where type =~ "microsoft.insights/datacollectionrules"
| extend DcrName = name, DcrId = id, DceId = tostring(properties.dataCollectionEndpointId)
| mv-expand DataFlow = properties.dataFlows
| extend OutputStream = tostring(DataFlow.outputStream)
| where OutputStream startswith "Custom-"
| mv-expand FlowDestination = DataFlow.destinations
| mv-expand LogDestination = properties.destinations.logAnalytics
| where tostring(FlowDestination) == tostring(LogDestination.name)
| where tostring(LogDestination.workspaceResourceId) =~ "{Workspace}"
| extend name = substring(OutputStream, 7)
| summarize ExistingDcrCount = dcount(DcrId), DcrNames = make_set(DcrName) by name
| extend ExistingDcrNames = strcat_array(DcrNames, ", ")
| project-away DcrNames

content.json:
## 2. Migrate or verify the selected table
Live subtype: **{SelectedTableSubTypeLive}**. Classic tables cannot be DCR output destinations until the table migrate operation enables DCR-based custom-log features.

### Migration impact - read before continuing
- Migration is **one-way**.
- MMA custom text logs can no longer write to the migrated table.
- Existing HTTP Data Collector API ingestion may continue only for existing columns; schema changes can break legacy ingestion.
- Stop legacy senders and switch to the Logs Ingestion API as part of the same change window.

The action requires `Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces/tables/migrate/action`, included in the **Log Analytics Contributor** role.

armActionContext.title: Migrate {SelectedTableName}
armActionContext.description: This one-way operation converts **{SelectedTableName}** from a Classic custom table to a DCR-based custom table. Confirm that MMA custom text collection is no longer required and that legacy HTTP Data Collector API senders are ready to be replaced.
armActionContext.resultMessage: Migration request for {SelectedTableName} completed. Refresh the Step 1 inventory and reselect the table to continue.

content.json: **After migration succeeds:** use the **Refresh** button on the Step 1 inventory and reselect `{SelectedTableName}`. The table remains in the unified inventory with its new subtype.
**Ready:** `{SelectedTableName}` is already DCR-capable. Continue to inspect its schema and any DCRs currently targeting it.

links.linkLabel: Next: reveal schema and existing DCRs below

content.json:
# 3 | Inspect schema and existing DCRs
Review the proposed input mapping and confirm whether another DCR already targets **{SelectedTableName}**.

## 3. Inspect the table schema and existing DCRs
This reads the *live* column list for the selected table and computes:
- **CleanName** - the column name with any legacy type-suffix removed.
- **MappedType** - the KQL/DCR data type for that input column.
- Whether two or more columns collapse to the same `CleanName` (a **collision**).
- **InputName** - the actual DCR input column. If any collision exists, the workbook safely retains all original unique names instead of blocking deployment.

content.title: Current columns -> DCR input-stream mapping

parameters.query: print value = tolower(tostring("{TableDcrReady}" == "true" and isnotempty("{InputColumnsJson:base64}")))

content.json: **Legacy V1 evidence:** `{LegacySuffixColumnCount}` non-system column(s) use a recognized legacy type suffix. For a DCR-based table, this is evidence that the schema may have originated from Classic ingestion, but Azure does not expose durable pre-migration history.

**Compatibility mode applied:** {CollisionCount} clean column name(s) are ambiguous (for example, `Computer_s` and `Computer_d` both become `Computer`). The source table cannot be changed, so the generated DCR input stream retains the table's original unique column names for every field. No table schema change is required, and deployment can continue. Your Logs Ingestion API payload must use the original suffixed names shown in **InputName**. To use clean names instead, resolve the ambiguity in the sending application before calling the API.

parameters.name: ExistingDcrCount
parameters.query:
resources
| where type =~ "microsoft.insights/datacollectionrules"
| mv-expand DataFlow = properties.dataFlows
| where tostring(DataFlow.outputStream) =~ strcat("Custom-", "{SelectedTableName}")
| mv-expand FlowDestination = DataFlow.destinations
| mv-expand LogDestination = properties.destinations.logAnalytics
| where tostring(FlowDestination) == tostring(LogDestination.name)
| where tostring(LogDestination.workspaceResourceId) =~ "{Workspace}"
| summarize Count = dcount(id)
| project value = tostring(Count)

content.query:
resources
| where type =~ "microsoft.insights/datacollectionrules"
| extend DcrName = name, DcrResourceId = id, DceResourceId = tostring(properties.dataCollectionEndpointId)
| mv-expand DataFlow = properties.dataFlows
| where tostring(DataFlow.outputStream) =~ strcat("Custom-", "{SelectedTableName}")
| mv-expand FlowDestination = DataFlow.destinations
| mv-expand LogDestination = properties.destinations.logAnalytics
| where tostring(FlowDestination) == tostring(LogDestination.name)
| where tostring(LogDestination.workspaceResourceId) =~ "{Workspace}"
| project ['DCR name'] = DcrName, ['DCR resource ID'] = DcrResourceId, ['DCE resource ID'] = DceResourceId, ['Input streams'] = strcat_array(DataFlow.streams, ", "), ['Transformation'] = tostring(DataFlow.transformKql), ['Output stream'] = tostring(DataFlow.outputStream)

content.json: **Existing DCR detected:** `{ExistingDcrCount}` DCR(s) already target this table in the selected workspace. Review them above before creating another rule; overlapping senders can duplicate ingestion.

# 4 | Configure the DCR
The input schema is ready. Configure the DCR and choose whether to create or reuse a Data Collection Endpoint.

## 4. Configure the Data Collection Rule
The DCR is created in the **same resource group and region as the workspace** (`{ResourceGroupId}`, `{WorkspaceLocation}`), per Azure Monitor recommended practice. Choose a name, and either create a new Data Collection Endpoint (DCE) or reuse one that already exists in the resource group.

# 5 | Review and deploy
Open the native ARM deployment to review the hosted template before deploying **{DcrName}**.

## 5. Review & deploy
Use **Review and Deploy Data Collection Rule** to open Azure's native ARM deployment experience. Select **View template** to inspect the hosted template and substituted parameters before deploying the Data Collection Rule and, if selected, a new Data Collection Endpoint.

links.linkLabel: Review and Deploy Data Collection Rule

templateRunContext.title: Deploy Data Collection Rule and Endpoint
templateRunContext.description: The template deploys **{DcrName}** and, when requested, **{NewDceName}** into `{ResourceGroupId}`. Use **View template** to inspect the resources and parameter values before deployment. No changes are made to the destination schema for `{SelectedTableName}`.

links.linkLabel: Review and Deploy Data Collection Rule

templateRunContext.title: Deploy Data Collection Rule and Endpoint
templateRunContext.description: The template deploys **{DcrName}** using the selected existing DCE into `{ResourceGroupId}`. Use **View template** to inspect the resources and parameter values before deployment. No changes are made to the destination schema for `{SelectedTableName}`.

content.json: **Note:** You need `Microsoft.Insights/dataCollectionRules/write` (and, if creating a new DCE, `Microsoft.Insights/dataCollectionEndpoints/write`) permission on the resource group to deploy - for example via the **Monitoring Contributor** built-in role. After deployment, update your ingestion client to call the [Logs ingestion API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/logs-ingestion-api-overview) against this DCR instead of the legacy HTTP Data Collector API.
